intro: Paper results compare MDOC with single-robot planners and evaluate MDOC-CBS on multi-robot coordination and larger maps.

figures.title: Single-robot narrow passages
figures.alt: Paper trajectory comparison for CEM, MPPI, RRT star, and MDOC on Narrow and More-Constrained Narrow maps.
figures.caption: Best collision-free trajectories from CEM, MPPI, RRT*, and MDOC on the Narrow (left) and More-Constrained Narrow (right) maps. These are the path-comparison panels from the paper; planner colors and legends are unchanged.

figures.title: Multi-robot coordination
figures.alt: Six-robot Conveyor Circle trajectories for KCBS, MMD-CBS, and MDOC-CBS, in that order.
figures.caption: Six robots in the Conveyor Circle setup: KCBS (left), MMD-CBS (center), and MDOC-CBS (right). Trajectories are shown without post-smoothing.

figures.title: Scaling to 40 robots
figures.alt: Success rate and planning time versus robot count on the 6 by 6 Empty map, with the original five-planner legend.
figures.caption: Success rate and planning time on the 6 × 6 Empty map with the Random setup and horizon H = 196. Ten seeded trials per method and map; each trial has a 500-second limit. Planning time is averaged over successful trials, with outliers included in the mean but omitted beyond the 95th percentile from the visualization.

tables.title: Useful samples through narrow passages
tables.caption: Pass & Free Yield (% ↑): candidate trajectories that both traverse the bottleneck and remain collision-free, under a fixed proposal budget of M = 128 per planning step.
notes: Ten trials per method and map, with different random seeds. Hardware: NVIDIA RTX A4500 (20 GB) and 12 CPU cores.

For RRT*, Pass & Free Yield is the fraction of expanded nodes whose associated paths traverse the bottleneck and remain collision-free; for trajectory optimizers it is the fraction of candidate trajectories.
Values and uncertainty are reproduced at the precision reported in the paper. The source caption does not identify the type of the ± uncertainty.
